mainTopic: When a woman may blame a stain on another source (size, louse, handled items, colors), why כתמים are rabbinic, and the dispute over רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's examination cloth
overview: The גמרא first defends רב הונא: a ברייתא about small and large drops treats a stain exactly the size of a גריס as one of the larger ones. Next, רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי argue about a stain slightly bigger than a גריס with a squashed louse on the extra part. רבי חנינא says טמאה. רבי ינאי says טהורה, because the visible louse explains the extra blood. רבי ירמיה then asks about a woman who handled something the size of a גריס and found a stain slightly bigger. A ברייתא ('a small item cannot explain a large stain') is pushed away as a proof, and his question is not answered. רבא rules that one kind of stain can explain several kinds, and the גמרא defends his rule in two versions against the ברייתא about red and black. רבינא explains that the laws of כתמים are a rabbinic strictness, so the חכמים could be lenient within them. Finally, שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק about the examination cloth proves that the חכמים disagree with him, and the chapter הרואה כתם ends.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to put a גריס-sized stain in the smaller group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about small and large drops and reads it as saying a stain exactly the size of a גריס can be blamed on a louse, which would go against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman had both smaller drops and larger drops of blood on her, she may blame them on an outside cause, even the larger one, up to the size of a גריס. Doesn't that mean a גריס-sized stain counts with the smaller drops?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and tries to read it as a challenge to רב הונא's view about a stain that is exactly the size of a גריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says she may blame even the 'upper' (bigger) drop on an outside cause 'up to a גריס'. The גמרא suggests that a גריס-sized drop belongs with the 'lower' (smaller) drops, so it too may be blamed on a louse. That would contradict רב הונא, who does not let a stain exactly the size of a גריס be blamed on a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: Drops of blood
She attributes, meaning she may blame the blood on an outside cause such as a louse, so she stays טהורה
The size of a split bean, the key size limit for blaming a stain on a louse
The upper one, meaning the bigger drop
What, is it not that...? A way of offering a reading that makes a proof or a challenge

phrases.english: If there were on her drops of blood below
phrases.notes: 'Below' here means smaller than a גריס, and 'above' in the next line means bigger.

phrases.english: and drops of blood above
she may attribute even the upper one, up to the size of a split bean
What, is it not that a split bean's size counts as from below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the דף about whether a stain exactly the size of a גריס may be blamed on a louse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that a stain exactly the size of a גריס is not blamed on a louse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא groups a גריס-sized drop with the small drops, then a גריס itself may be blamed on a louse, against רב הונא.

steps.title: No, a גריס-sized stain belongs to the larger group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading: a stain exactly the size of a גריס counts with the larger drops, so the ברייתא fits רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A גריס-sized stain counts as one of the upper, larger drops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Up to a גריס' means up to but not including a גריס. A stain exactly the size of a גריס is grouped with the bigger drops, which may not be blamed on a louse. So the ברייתא does not contradict רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: From above, meaning in the bigger group

phrases.english: No, a split bean's size counts as from above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גריס-sized drop belongs with the small drops and may be blamed on a louse.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גריס-sized drop belongs with the large drops, so רב הונא stands.
steps.whatToRemember: After this answer, the ברייתא fits רב הונא: a stain exactly the size of a גריס is treated like a bigger stain, so it is not blamed on a louse. Only stains smaller than a גריס are.

steps.title: A stain slightly bigger than a גריס with a squashed louse on it
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a stain slightly bigger than a גריס, with a squashed louse on the extra part. רבי חנינא says טמאה; רבי ינאי says טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a stain was found on her that was a גריס and a bit more, and on that extra bit a louse was squashed. רבי חנינא says she is טמאה; רבי ינאי says she is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת between רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי about a stain just over the size of a גריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a stain bigger than a גריס cannot be blamed on a louse. Here, though, there is an actual squashed louse in the extra part, which may explain that extra blood. The question is whether that changes the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a split bean and a bit more
Squashed or crushed
A louse
Ritually impure
Ritually pure

phrases.english: It was stated: there was found on her a stain the size of a split bean and a bit more,
and in that extra bit a louse was squashed.
Rabbi Ḥanina says: she is impure,
Rabbi Yannai says: she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that a stain bigger than a גריס is not blamed on a louse, and asks about a case with a visible louse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: טמאה. רבי ינאי: טהורה.

steps.title: Why רבי חנינא says טמאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא's reason: a stain is blamed on a louse only up to a גריס, never when it is more than a גריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says טמאה, because she may blame a stain on a louse only when it is a גריס, not when it is a גריס and more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי חנינא's strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנינא, the size limit is firm. Once the stain is bigger than a גריס, it may not be blamed on a louse, even though there is a squashed louse on part of it.

keyTerms.meaning: She attributes, meaning she blames it on another cause

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina says she is impure,
because she may attribute only with a stain the size of a split bean;
phrases.notes: 'The size of a split bean' here means up to that size, the normal limit for blaming a stain on a louse.

phrases.english: with a split bean and a bit more, she may not attribute.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר טְמֵאָה כִּי תָּלְיָא בְּכִגְרִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion in the מחלוקת of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גריס limit is absolute; any stain larger than a גריס is טמא.

steps.title: Why רבי ינאי says טהורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's reason: the visible louse explains the extra blood. Take it away and only a גריס is left, which can be blamed on another louse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי says טהורה. The rule against blaming more than a גריס applies only where no louse is squashed in it. But where a louse is squashed in it, it is clear that the extra bit is louse blood. That leaves a stain of a גריס. Since a stain like that is normally blamed on a louse, here too she may blame it on one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי ינאי's lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי agrees that a stain bigger than a גריס normally cannot be blamed on a louse. Here, though, the squashed louse proves where the extra blood came from. Once that part is removed, the rest is a normal-size stain that can be blamed on a second louse.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to... It limits a rule to certain cases
The matter is evident, meaning it is clear from what we see
What is left is...
In general, in a normal case

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says: she is pure,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי — הֵיכָא דְּלֹא רְצוּפָה בּוֹ מַאֲכוֹלֶת,
phrases.english: since that rule applies only where no louse is squashed in it,
but where a louse is squashed in it,
it is evident that this extra bit
is the blood of a louse;
what remains is the size of a split bean,
and since in general she may attribute such a stain,
here too she may attribute it.
phrases.notes: She blames the rest of the stain on a second louse that she cannot see.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אוֹמֵר: טְהוֹרָה, הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion, in contrast to רבי חנינא's reasoning in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A visible squashed louse accounts for the extra blood, so the remaining גריס can still be blamed on a louse.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ינאי does not say a stain bigger than a גריס can be blamed on one louse. He removes the extra part because the visible louse explains it, and then blames the rest, a stain of a גריס, on another louse.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא: more than a גריס is always טמא. רבי ינאי: if a visible louse explains the extra part, subtract it and judge what is left.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about a woman who handled something the size of a גריס
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: if she was busy with something the size of a גריס and then found a stain slightly bigger than a גריס, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if she was busy with something the size of a גריס, and then a stain a גריס and a bit more was found on her, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה raises a new question that builds on the מחלוקת of רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is a known outside source of blood, but it is only the size of a גריס, while the stain is slightly bigger. He asks whether she may blame the stain on what she handled, even though the stain is larger than that source.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that needs an answer
She was busy with, meaning she handled something that could leave blood on her
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
if she was busy with something the size of a split bean,
phrases.notes: For example, blood from a bird she slaughtered, which could leave a stain on her.

phrases.english: and a stain the size of a split bean and a bit more was found on her, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the מחלוקת of steps 3 to 5 and applies it to a new case, with a known outside source that is only a גריס in size.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a stain slightly larger than a גריס may be blamed on a known outside source that was only the size of a גריס.

steps.title: The question works according to both רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה points out that his question can be asked according to רבי חנינא and also according to רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to רבי חנינא, and it can be asked according to רבי ינאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה shows that his question is not settled by either side of the earlier מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His new case is different from the louse case in two ways. There is a known outside source, but nothing visible proves that the extra blood came from it. So even רבי חנינא might be lenient here, and even רבי ינאי might be strict, and the question stays open for both.

keyTerms.meaning: The question can be asked, meaning the question applies according to this view

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to Rabbi Ḥanina,
and it can be asked according to Rabbi Yannai.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּבְעֵי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, תִּבְעֵי לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far רבי ירמיה's question reaches: it applies to both sides of the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How each of רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי would rule in the case of a known outside source the size of a גריס.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the reasons each אמורא gave for the louse case do not automatically settle a case with a different kind of evidence.

steps.title: The question according to רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי חנינא, who said טמאה, may have meant only a case where she was not busy with anything. Here she was, so maybe she can blame the stain on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to רבי חנינא. He only said 'impure' where she had not been handling anything. But here she was handling something, so maybe she can blame the stain on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first side of רבי ירמיה's question. Maybe רבי חנינא would be lenient here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חנינא's case, the only possible cause for the extra blood was a louse, and a louse cannot explain more than a גריס. Here she actually handled something bloody. That is a real, known source, so maybe even רבי חנינא would allow blaming part of the stain on it.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling in a specific situation

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina only said
there, 'she is impure,'
phrases.notes: 'There' is the case from before: a stain a bit bigger than a גריס with a squashed louse on it.

phrases.english: only where she was not busy with anything,
but here, where she was busy with something,
she can attribute it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops step 7's claim that the question works according to רבי חנינא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does handling a real bloody item let her blame part of a stain slightly bigger than a גריס on it, even according to רבי חנינא?

steps.title: The question according to רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe even רבי ינאי, who said טהורה, was lenient only because a louse was visible on the stain. Here there is none, so maybe she cannot attribute.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe, even רבי ינאי, who said 'pure,' only meant it where a louse is squashed on the stain. Where no louse is squashed on it, she cannot attribute it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. Maybe even the lenient רבי ינאי would be strict here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי was lenient because the visible louse clearly explained the extra blood. Here nothing visible is on the stain. We cannot be sure what made which part, so maybe she cannot split the stain between the item and a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.whyThisMatters: The two sides show why the question is real. Each opinion has a reason to go the 'other' way in this new case.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
even according to Rabbi Yannai, who said 'she is pure,'
that applies only where
a louse is squashed on it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּאֵין רְצוּפָה בּוֹ מַאֲכוֹלֶת
phrases.english: but where no louse is squashed on it
she cannot attribute it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי דְּאָמַר טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Without a visible louse, can she split the stain between the item she handled and a louse, even according to רבי ינאי?

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: a small item cannot explain a large stain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if she handled something red she cannot blame a black stain on it, and if she handled a small item she cannot blame a large stain on it. The גמרא suggests this is exactly רבי ירמיה's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if she handled something red, she cannot blame a black stain on it. If she handled something small, she cannot blame a large stain on it. What is the case? Is it not just like this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי ירמיה's question from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's second rule says a small source cannot explain a bigger stain. The גמרא suggests this means she handled a גריס and found a bit more than a גריס. If so, she cannot attribute and is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Attributes, blames the stain on a source
Red / black (stain colors)
Small amount / large amount
What is the case? How do we picture it?
Is it not a case just like this one?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If she was busy with something red,
she may not blame a black stain on it;
with a small amount, she may not blame a large stain on it.
What is the case?
Is it not a case like this one?!
phrases.notes: 'This one' is רבי ירמיה's case: she handled a גריס and found a stain a bit bigger than a גריס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from steps 6–9.
steps.raayaObject: That in רבי ירמיה's case she cannot attribute the stain and is טמאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: if she handled a small amount, she cannot blame a large stain on it.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about a much bigger stain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא could be talking about a stain of two גריסין plus a bit, after she handled only one גריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where she handled a גריס-sized amount and found on herself a stain of two גריסין and a bit more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by placing the ברייתא in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stain is more than double what she handled, the ברייתא's rule does not touch רבי ירמיה's case. There the stain is only slightly bigger than the item, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as (the case is like this)
And a little more

phrases.english: No,
the case is where she was busy with a גריס-sized amount,
and a stain of two גריסין and a bit more was found on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question in steps 6–9 stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case where the stain is far more than double the item, not just slightly bigger.

steps.title: Then why would the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If the stain is two גריסין plus, it seems obvious she cannot attribute it. So why teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading of the ברייתא as too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take away one גריס for the item she handled. More than a גריס is still left, which is too much to blame on a louse. So she is clearly טמאה, and the ruling seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why say it? It is obvious

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as a stain of two גריסין plus a bit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After removing one גריס, more than a גריס remains, so the impurity is obvious. A ברייתא should not teach something obvious.

steps.title: We do not place the attributed part in the middle
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed. We might have thought to place the גריס she can attribute in the middle of the stain, leaving two small side pieces, each under the minimum size. The ברייתא teaches that she is still טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: take the גריס from the bird and put it in the middle. Then go to this side, and there is not a full measure. Go to that side, and there is not a full measure. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא blocks a clever way of splitting up the stain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the attributed גריס is imagined in the center, what is left is two separate pieces, each less than a גריס. Each piece alone could then be blamed on a louse. The ברייתא rejects this. The leftover is treated as one stain bigger than a גריס, so she is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Throw it into the middle
The minimum size that matters for the law
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Whatever she cannot attribute to what she handled is measured as one stain. We do not split it into small pieces to keep each one under a גריס. The ברייתא was pushed away as proof, so רבי ירמיה's question is still unanswered.
steps.confusionAlert: 'זיל הכא… זיל הכא' is the mistaken idea that the ברייתא rejects. It is not the ruling. The ruling is קא משמע לן: she is impure.

phrases.english: You might have said:
take the גריס-sized part (from the bird),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word 'bird' in round brackets. It means the bloody item she handled.

phrases.english: and put it in the middle;
go to this side, and there is no full measure,
go to that side, and there is no full measure,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the ruling blocks a reasonable but wrong assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Place the attributed גריס in the center, so each leftover side piece is under a גריס and can be blamed on a louse.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not split the leftover this way. The rest counts as one stain bigger than a גריס, so she is טמאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for measuring what is left after attributing part of a stain. It also leaves רבי ירמיה's question without an answer from this ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: one kind of stain found on her covers many kinds
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if one type of stain is found on a woman, she may blame stains of several types on that same source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If one kind of stain was found on her, she may blame many kinds of stains on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבא. If a woman has one stain clearly from a known non-blood source, she may blame other stains of different colors on that source too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a lenient rule. Once we know something was sprayed on her without her noticing, we can say the other stains came the same way, even if their colors are different.

keyTerms.meaning: One type or kind (of stain)
She blames, or attributes, the stain to a source other than her body
Several different kinds or colors

phrases.english: Rava said:
If one kind was found on her,
phrases.notes: He means one kind of stain from a known source, like tree sap, found on her body or clothes.

phrases.english: she may attribute several kinds to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: נִמְצָא עָלֶיהָ מִין אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule about attributing stains, after the discussion of size in steps 10-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain of one type found on her lets her attribute stains of several types to that source.

steps.title: Challenge from the red and black ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from the ברייתא that says a woman who handled something red cannot blame a black stain on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If she handled something red, she cannot blame a black stain on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule using the ברייתא from step 10. That ברייתא says a different color cannot be blamed on the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא allows many colors to be blamed on one source. The ברייתא seems to say the color has to match. So the two seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If she was occupied with something red,
she may not attribute a black stain to it!
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא quoted back in step 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that one kind of stain lets her blame many kinds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a black stain cannot be blamed on a red source, so different colors should not be blamed on one source.

steps.title: Handling something is a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a woman who handled a red item is a different case from רבא's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: A case where she handled something is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by saying the ברייתא is about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, she knows she handled a red thing, so only red stains make sense from it. In רבא's case, she did not handle anything; something got sprayed on her without her knowing. If one kind landed on her unnoticed, other kinds could have too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different

phrases.english: Where she was occupied with something, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about red and black seemed to cover רבא's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a known item she handled. רבא is about a stain found on her with no known handling.

steps.title: Second version: handling one kind covers many kinds
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רבא rules that if she handled one type of thing, she may blame stains of several types on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא said: If she handled one kind of thing, she may blame many kinds of stains on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of רבא's rule. In this version, his rule is about a woman who actually handled something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבא's case is the same kind of case as the ברייתא, since she handled something. So the answer from step 16 will not work, and a new answer is needed.

phrases.english: Some say: Rava said:
If she was occupied with one kind,
she may attribute several kinds to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: נִתְעַסְּקָה בְּמִין אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's rule from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handling one type of item lets her attribute stains of several types to it.

steps.title: Same challenge against the second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version from the same ברייתא about red and black.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If she handled something red, she cannot blame a black stain on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא is used against the second version of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the challenge is stronger. Both רבא and the ברייתא talk about a woman who handled something, so we cannot say the cases are different the way step 16 did.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If she was occupied with something red,
she may not attribute a black stain to it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of רבא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says handling a red item does not let her blame a black stain, so handling one kind should not cover many kinds.

steps.title: רבא meant a chicken with several kinds of blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא was talking about a woman who handled a chicken, which has several kinds of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא said this, he meant that she handled a chicken, which has several kinds of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבא's rule to a special case: an item that itself has blood of different colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughtered chicken has blood of different shades. So even though she handled only one item, that item could make stains of several colors. A red item, though, can only make red stains, which is why the ברייתא is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: A chicken
Several kinds of blood

phrases.english: When Rava said this,
it was where she was occupied with a chicken,
which has several kinds of blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא seemed to say handling any one item covers stains of any color.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא only meant an item like a chicken that really has several kinds of blood.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, a stain can only be blamed on a source that could really have made it. A red item cannot explain a black stain, but a chicken with several kinds of blood can explain several colors.

steps.title: Were stain laws made to be lenient or strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's story where רבי עקיבא said the stain laws were made to be lenient, and challenges it from a ברייתא that says they were made to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה tells a story about a woman who came to רבי עקיבא, and he said the חכמים made this law to be lenient. But a ברייתא teaches: The חכמים did not say this to be lenient, but to be strict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's story about רבי עקיבא. It points out that a ברייתא seems to say the exact opposite of what he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא made a woman טהורה and explained that the laws of כתמים were made to be lenient. The ברייתא says these laws were made to be strict. These seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident
To be lenient
To be strict

phrases.english: "There was an incident involving a woman, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's story where רבי עקיבא made the woman טהורה. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת הַדָּבָר לְהָקֵל
phrases.english: The Sages did not state this matter to be lenient,
but to be strict!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה וְהָתַנְיָא: לֹא אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת הַדָּבָר לְהָקֵל אֶלָּא לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new part of the משנה, the story of רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה that the stain laws were made to be lenient.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the stain laws were made to be strict, the opposite of רבי עקיבא's words.

steps.title: רבינא: strict compared to the Torah, but still only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the laws of כתמים are stricter than the Torah, but since they are only rabbinic, the חכמים could be lenient in specific cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The law was not made to be more lenient than Torah law, but to be stricter than Torah law. And stains themselves are only rabbinic, so there is room for leniency.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the contradiction by showing that both statements are true, each in a different sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא means the whole idea of stain impurity adds strictness beyond the Torah, where stains would not make her טמאה. רבי עקיבא means that because this impurity is only דרבנן, the חכמים were willing to be lenient in doubtful cases, like the woman in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah law
Blood stains found on a woman's body or clothes
Rabbinic law, not from the Torah itself

steps.whatToRemember: The laws of כתמים are a rabbinic strictness added on top of Torah law. Since they are only דרבנן, the חכמים allow leniencies in doubtful cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why so many rulings in this perek lean lenient: the whole category of כתמים is rabbinic, so doubts can be decided leniently.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Not to be more lenient than Torah law,
but rather to be stricter than Torah law.
And stains themselves are by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: לֹא לְהָקֵל עַל דִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different senses of the same idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא and the ברייתא seemed to disagree about whether stain laws are lenient or strict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stain laws are stricter than Torah law, which is what the ברייתא means. Since they are rabbinic, leniency is allowed within them, which is what רבי עקיבא means.

steps.title: Do the חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of an examination cloth and asks whether the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the case in the משנה of an examination cloth that was placed under the pillow, a question was asked: do the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and opens a question. It wants to know whether רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's view is a lone opinion or one everyone agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says that a round stain on the cloth is טהור and a long, drawn-out one is טמא. The משנה does not record anyone arguing with him, so the גמרא asks whether the חכמים actually hold differently. This question sets up the two proofs that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: An examination cloth a woman uses to check herself
A question was raised before them (an open question the גמרא tries to settle)
Do they disagree?

phrases.english: An examination cloth that was placed,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the cloth was put under her pillow and blood was found on it later.

phrases.english: a question was asked before them:
Do the Rabbis disagree
with Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: moves from the general stain discussion to the משנה's case of the examination cloth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכמים dispute רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's rule that a long stain on an examination cloth is טמא no matter its size.

steps.title: Attempted proof from stains that combine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says long stains combine to reach the minimum size. That cannot fit רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, who needs no minimum for a long stain, so it seems to be the חכמים, which would show they disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a long stain combines with other stains, but separate drops do not combine. Whose view is this? If it is רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's, why would combining be needed? He said a long stain of any size is טמא! So it must be the חכמים. Doesn't that prove they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove that the חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says long stains 'combine', meaning they only count once together they reach the minimum size. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק said any long stain is טמא even if it is tiny, so for him combining would be pointless. That makes the ברייתא look like the חכמים, who would then be holding that a long stain still needs the minimum size.

keyTerms.meaning: A bloodstain found on a garment or the body (not on an examination cloth)
Combines / combining: adding small stains together to reach the minimum size
Drawn out, elongated (a long stain rather than a round drop)
Whose view is this?
Learn from it (a proof is being drawn)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a long stain combines,
phrases.notes: Several long stains can be added together to reach the minimum size of a stain that makes her טמאה.

phrases.english: separate drops do not combine.
Whose view is this?
If it is Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok,
why do I need combining?
He said, 'A long stain of any size is impure'!
Rather, is it not the Rabbis,
and learn from it that they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First attempt to answer the question of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying long stains combine, which only makes sense if a long stain needs a minimum size.

steps.title: His rule was only about an examination cloth
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא could be רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק after all, because his 'any size' rule applies only to an examination cloth, not to an ordinary stain.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא really is רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק. When he said a long stain of any size is טמא, he meant on an examination cloth. For an ordinary stain he did not say that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא by limiting רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a כתם, an ordinary stain, while רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק spoke about an עד, an examination cloth. So he can agree that ordinary long stains need the minimum size and can combine. The ברייתא therefore does not prove anyone disagrees with him. The next step brings a different proof that settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in fact (keeping the original reading against the proof)
And when he said (introduces a limit on someone's statement)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up עד and כתם here. An עד is a cloth used on purpose to check herself; a כתם is a stain found on clothing. The whole answer depends on treating these two differently.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק,
phrases.english: No, it really is Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק —
phrases.english: and when Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok spoke,
it was about an examination cloth, but about an ordinary stain, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's 'any size' rule covers ordinary stains, but it applies only to an examination cloth.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל's ruling: they disagree
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules הלכה like רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק. A ruling like that implies that others disagree, so the חכמים do argue with him. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, 'The הלכה is like רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.' If he needed to say 'the הלכה is like him,' that shows others disagree. Learn from it: they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof, and this one settles the question: the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only decide whose view is the הלכה when there is a dispute. If everyone agreed with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, שמואל would have nothing to decide. So his ruling shows there is an opposing view, and the גמרא accepts the proof with 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows so-and-so
This implies that they disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים do disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק about the examination cloth, and the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method of the גמרא: a ruling of 'הלכה like X' is itself evidence that there was a dispute.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halakha is like Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok.
Saying 'the halakha is' implies that they disagree,
learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in step 24, a second proof resolves the question of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling 'הלכה כרבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק', which only makes sense if there is a dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, and the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of הרואה כתם
steps.stepSummary: The chapter about stains, called הרואה כתם, is formally finished with the words הדרן עלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter of הרואה כתם.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter הרואה כתם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chapter is named by its opening words, and this one began with the משנה about a woman who sees a כתם. Saying הדרן עלך means 'we will come back to you,' a promise to return and learn this chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a chapter
A blood stain found on a woman's body or clothing, which can make her טמאה by rabbinic law
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא, named after its opening words

steps.whatToRemember: This chapter taught that the laws of כתמים are rabbinic. Because of that, the חכמים were stricter than the Torah in some ways and lenient in specific cases. It ended with the conclusion that the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק about an examination cloth, and that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, as שמואל ruled.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
[chapter] 'One who sees a stain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 settled that the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק, the chapter formally closes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter of הרואה כתם is complete. The learner promises to return to it.
